user_query: My husband is violent. I want a divorce.
variations: My spouse hit me. What can I do?
How do I get protection from my husband?
part_a_general_info: If you are in immediate danger, call the Police at 999. You can apply for a Personal Protection Order (PPO) at the Family Justice Courts. A Domestic Exclusion Order (DEO) can also prevent the abuser from entering the home. Unreasonable behaviour including violence is a ground for divorce. You may not need to wait 3 years if exceptional hardship can be shown. PPO and divorce are separate proceedings. You can pursue both concurrently. Support: AWARE, PAVE, National Anti-Violence Helpline (1800-777-0000).
triage_questions: Q1: Are you currently in immediate danger?
Q2: What is the nature and frequency of the violence?
Q3: Do you have a safe place to stay? Are children safe?
Q4: Have you made a police report or sought medical attention?
Q5: Have you applied for a PPO before?
branching_logic: If Q1 = YES → Priority: Call 999. Do not proceed until safety established.
If Q3 = no safe place → Refer to crisis shelters first.
If Q5 = existing PPO breached → Inform breach is criminal offence, report to police.
routing: Route A (Immediate danger): Call 999. Refer to crisis shelters. Legal referrals secondary.
Route B (No PPO yet): Refer to FJC for PPO. Refer to PBSG Family Law clinic. Refer to AWARE/PAVE.
Route C (PPO breached): Report breach to police. Commence divorce if not yet filed.
Route D (Violence + divorce): PPO concurrent with divorce. Violence may justify early filing (<3 years).
guardrail: Must NOT assess severity or credibility of allegations. Safety referrals and general information only.
